<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Confront the commit message with the format the changelog will read.

```text
Reads the message file (the one git passes to the commit-msg hook) and confronts
the subject with Conventional Commits.

The changelog is born from the commits. A subject outside the format does not vanish from the history —
it vanishes from the CHANGELOG, and it is only discovered when someone goes to generate the first version and
what is missing is already hundreds of commits away.

Messages generated by git (merge, revert, fixup) pass: nobody wrote them.
```

## Uso

```bash
anchors commit-msg <file>
```

## Changelog e pull requests — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors changelog`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/changelog/) | Build the technical changelog from the commits, release by release |
| **`anchors commit-msg`** | Confront the commit message with the format the changelog will read |
| [`anchors pr-body`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/pr-body/) | Write the lines linking this work's cards, in the platform's syntax |
| [`anchors backfill-labels`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/backfill-labels/) | Write into open issues the links the new version began to mark |
| [`anchors report`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/report/) | Generate reports in docs/ by perspective (cuts of what Anchors measures) |

<!-- cli-reference:end -->
